title: Low-rate purified-distance exponent for quantum privacy amplification
summary: Determine the exact purified-distance security exponent of quantum privacy amplification at extraction rates below the source's critical rate.

formal_statement.body: For an admissible i.i.d. cq state $\rho_{XE}^{\otimes n}$ and source-model hash $f_n:X^n\to Z_n$ of rate $R<R_{\mathrm{critical}}$, determine the exact optimal exponent of the purified distance $P(\rho_{Z_nE^n}^{f_n},\tau_{Z_n}\otimes\rho_E^{\otimes n})$. Prove matching achievability and converse exponents for every admissible source and every rate below its critical rate.

scope.domain: Quantum-proof privacy amplification measured by purified distance in the low-rate regime
assumptions: $\rho_{XE}$ and the hash model follow the source's privacy-amplification theorems
Security is measured by purified distance
scope.unresolved_remainder: The source proves the exact high-rate exponent but demonstrates that its available bounds are not tight in general below $R_{\mathrm{critical}}$. No inspected later public result supplies matching low-rate purified-distance bounds over the full domain.

progress.summary: The source determines the purified-distance exponent above a critical rate and explicitly leaves the complementary low-rate exponent open.
